instructions: Put the rice on first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice, then add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Bring it to a boil, cover, turn the heat to its lowest setting and cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on and take it off the heat until the curry is ready.

Meanwhile, cut the potatoes into 3/4-inch chunks and slice the carrots into 1/4-inch coins. Finely chop the onion, mince the garlic cloves and grate the ginger. Roughly chop the peanuts and about 1/4 cup of the cilantro.
Heat the oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium. Add the onion and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and just starting to turn gold.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and cinnamon and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the curry paste and stir it into the onion. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it darkens and smells strong. Don't rush this part. It's where the flavor starts.
Add the potatoes and carrots and stir for 1 minute, until they're coated in the paste.
Add both cans of coconut milk, the broth, 2 tbsp peanut butter, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp sugar. Stir until the peanut butter melts in, then bring it to a gentle simmer.

Turn the heat to medium-low, cover with the lid slightly open and cook for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until a fork slides into the potatoes easily. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in half of the chopped peanuts and the juice of the lime.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice, topped with the rest of the peanuts and the chopped cilantro.
method_notes: No vegetable massaman with 20 or more ratings was readable, so there is no qualifying lead. The lead is Vegan with Gusto (page shows 5 stars from 1 vote; JSON-LD not shown). Well Plated (chicken) and RecipeTin Eats (beef, a trusted cook) were also read for ratios and order but are different dishes, so they are not listed as sources: bloom the paste with aromatics, then potatoes, carrots and about 2 cans of coconut milk, peanut butter for body, a sweet and salty finish, lime off the heat. All agree on potatoes and peanuts; they differ on paste (jar versus made from scratch) and how much liquid. Changed: soy sauce takes the place of fish sauce, no green beans, and the jar paste must be checked for shrimp paste before it goes in the basket.
